blogPosts.title: How Much Does Attic Storage Cost in Melbourne? A Complete Guide for 2026
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about attic storage costs in Southbank and Melbourne? We break down pricing for Essential Attic, Clean-Air Attic and Premium Attic Room packages.
body: If you're a homeowner in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne, you've probably looked up at that empty roof space and wondered what it would cost to turn it into usable storage. The truth is, attic storage pricing varies widely depending on the size of your cavity, the type of solution you choose, and the finishes you want. In this guide, we'll break down the costs for the three main tiers: Essential Attic, Clean-Air Attic, and Premium Attic Room, so you can budget with confidence.

At the entry level, an Essential Attic typically includes a safe attic ladder and strong particle board flooring laid over your ceiling joists. This is a practical, budget-friendly option for general household storage — think Christmas decorations, suitcases, and seasonal gear. For a standard Melbourne home with a roof cavity around 30 square metres, you can expect to pay anywhere from $2,500 to $4,500 installed. The final price depends on the complexity of access and any additional materials needed.

The Clean-Air Attic is a step up. It adds dust-proof wall lining, battening, and kickboards to create a sealed environment that keeps dust, insulation fibres, and pests away from your stored items. This is ideal for clothing, keepsakes, and anything you want to keep pristine. Prices for a Clean-Air Attic in Southbank typically range from $4,500 to $7,000. The lining material and roof pitch can affect the cost, so a free onsite measure is essential for an accurate quote.

For homeowners seeking the ultimate in attic storage, the Premium Attic Room offers plastered walls and ceiling, a polished finish, and optional upgrades like carpet, skylights, and air vents. This is a true room conversion that can double as a home office or guest space. Prices start from around $8,000 and can go up to $15,000 or more depending on the features. Skylights alone add $800 to $2,000 each, but they flood the space with natural light and make it feel infinitely more usable.

Beyond the base package, additional costs can include electrical work for lighting and powerpoints (around $300-$600 per point), ventilation fans ($200-$500), and custom shelving ($200-$1,000). In older Melbourne homes with irregular roof structures, you may need extra structural work, which our team assesses during the free measure. We always provide a fixed, itemised quote before work begins — no surprises.

Finally, remember that attic storage is one of the most cost-effective ways to add usable space to your home without the expense and disruption of a full extension. In Melbourne's competitive property market, a well-finished attic can also boost your home's resale value. Whether you're in Southbank, St Kilda, or Richmond, Ashford Attics provides a free, no-obligation measure and quote to help you understand exactly what your attic needs and what it will cost.

blogPosts.title: Choosing the Right Attic Ladder for Your Melbourne Home
blogPosts.excerpt: Not all attic ladders are the same. Find out which type suits your Southbank home's ceiling height, roof pitch, and storage needs.
body: When you decide to turn your roof space into storage, the first step is getting safe and convenient access. The attic ladder is the gateway to your new storage area, and choosing the right one is crucial for both safety and usability. Melbourne homes vary enormously in ceiling height and roof pitch, so there's no one-size-fits-all solution. In this guide, we'll walk you through the main types of attic ladders and how to pick the best one for your Southbank home.

The most common type is the folding attic ladder, which folds into sections and slides down from a ceiling hatch. These are compact and work well for standard ceiling heights (2.4 to 2.7 metres). They're typically made from aluminium or timber, with aluminium being lighter and more durable in Melbourne's variable climate. A good folding ladder will have non-slip steps and a sturdy handrail. Prices range from $300 to $800 installed.

For higher ceilings — common in newer apartment buildings or heritage homes in Southbank — a telescopic ladder is a great option. These extend like a telescope and retract neatly into the hatch. They're very space-efficient and can reach up to 3 metres or more. Telescopic ladders are usually aluminium and are popular for their sleek design. Expect to pay between $400 and $900 installed, depending on the reach and weight capacity.

If you plan to use your attic frequently or store heavy items, consider a drop-down staircase. These are more substantial, with wooden treads and a handrail on both sides. They feel like a real staircase and provide the safest access. However, they require more headroom and a larger hatch opening. Drop-down staircases are ideal for Premium Attic Rooms where regular access is expected. Prices start from $1,200 and can go up to $2,500 installed.

Another factor is the roof pitch. In Melbourne, many older homes have steep roof pitches that limit the space available for the ladder mechanism. Our team at Ashford Attics assesses the roof cavity during the free measure to ensure the ladder fits properly and provides adequate head clearance. We also ensure the hatch is positioned for easy access without interfering with existing ceiling lights or structural beams.

Safety is paramount. All our ladders meet Australian standards (AS 1657) for strength and stability. We install them with proper fixing to the roof structure and include a locking mechanism to prevent accidental collapse. When you choose Ashford Attics, you get more than just a ladder — you get peace of mind that the access point is safe, durable, and seamlessly integrated into your ceiling. Contact us for a free measure and we'll recommend the best ladder for your Southbank home.

blogPosts.title: Benefits of a Clean-Air Attic for Melbourne's Climate
blogPosts.excerpt: Melbourne's dust and humidity can damage stored items. Discover how a Clean-Air Attic protects your belongings year-round.
body: Melbourne's climate is famously unpredictable — hot summers, cool winters, and plenty of wind. That dust, pollen, and moisture can find its way into your roof cavity and settle on everything you store. If you've ever pulled out a box of winter clothes from the attic and found them coated in fine dust or smelling musty, you know the problem. A Clean-Air Attic from Ashford Attics is designed specifically to combat these issues and keep your stored items in pristine condition.

The key feature of a Clean-Air Attic is the dust-proof wall lining. We install a continuous lining over the roof rafters and walls, creating a sealed barrier between your storage area and the insulation, roof tiles, and outside air. This prevents dust, insulation fibres, and even pests from entering the space. Combined with added battening and kickboards, the lining also gives the attic a clean, finished look — no more exposed insulation or rough timber.

Moisture control is another major benefit. Melbourne's humidity can cause mould and mildew to develop in enclosed spaces. Our Clean-Air Attic includes ventilation options such as roof vents or eaves vents to allow airflow while keeping dust out. This reduces condensation and keeps the environment dry. For extra protection, we can also install a vapour barrier. The result: your keepsakes, clothing, and documents stay dry and free from damage year-round.

Organisation is simpler too. With kickboards along the edges, you have a clear boundary to stack boxes and bins without them touching the roof lining. The smooth walls and floor make it easy to clean — just a quick vacuum or wipe down. Many of our Southbank clients use their Clean-Air Attic for storing off-season wardrobes, family heirlooms, and even wine (with proper temperature control).

From a home value perspective, a Clean-Air Attic is a smart investment. When you eventually sell your Melbourne home, having a clean, protected attic space that can be marketed as 'extra storage ready to use' is a strong selling point. It shows buyers that the home has been well-maintained and thoughtfully improved. Compared to a standard dusty attic, a Clean-Air Attic can add thousands to your property's perceived value.

If you're in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne and want to protect your belongings from dust, moisture and pests, talk to us about a Clean-Air Attic. We'll measure your roof space, discuss your storage needs, and provide a fixed quote. It's a relatively small investment that pays off every time you access your attic and find everything clean and organised.

blogPosts.title: How Skylights Transform Attic Spaces in Melbourne Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Adding natural light to your attic makes it brighter, more usable, and more valuable. Here's what Southbank homeowners need to know.
body: One of the most common complaints about attic storage is that it's dark and uninviting. A windowless roof space can feel cramped and unappealing, even if it's well-organised. That's where skylights come in. Installing a skylight in your attic can transform it from a forgotten storage void into a bright, functional room that you actually want to use. For Southbank homeowners considering a Premium Attic Room, skylights are often the finishing touch that makes all the difference.

There are several types of skylights suitable for Melbourne homes. The most popular is the fixed skylight — a simple window in the roof that lets in natural light. These are ideal for attics where you don't need ventilation (the attic already has its own vents). Fixed skylights are relatively affordable, with installation costs ranging from $800 to $1,500 depending on the size and roof material. They're also low-maintenance and very energy-efficient.

For attics that double as a living space or home office, a vented skylight is a great choice. It opens to allow fresh air to circulate, which can help regulate temperature on Melbourne's hot summer days. Vented skylights come with remote controls or manual crank mechanisms. Prices start from $1,200 and can go up to $2,500 for larger models with rain sensors. They add both light and airflow, making the attic comfortable year-round.

Another option is the tubular skylight, which uses a reflective tube to channel light from the roof into the room below. These are perfect for attics with limited roof space or where a standard skylight won't fit. Tubular skylights are very efficient and can illuminate up to 20 square metres. They cost around $600 to $1,000 installed and are a great way to bring natural light into a dark attic without major structural changes.

When installing skylights in an attic, it's important to consider roof pitch, orientation, and shading. North-facing skylights provide consistent light throughout the day, while west-facing ones can cause glare in the afternoon. Our team at Ashford Attics assesses your roof orientation and recommends the best placement to maximise light without overheating. We also ensure proper flashing and sealing to prevent leaks — critical in Melbourne's rainy winters.

If you're planning a Premium Attic Room in your Southbank home, adding one or two skylights can make the space feel like an entirely new room. Clients often tell us they start using their attic for hobbies, reading, or even as a guest bedroom once it's brightened up. Skylights also improve ventilation, reduce the need for artificial lighting, and boost the overall aesthetic of the space. Get in touch for a free quote and we'll help you choose the right skylight for your attic transformation.
